source.title: MedSAE: Dissecting MedCLIP Representations with Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Riccardo Renzulli; Colas Lepoutre; E. Cassano; Marco Grangetto

record.tranche_reason: It compares MedSAE features with raw MedCLIP embeddings using class-correlation entropy and automated image-based interpretation detection, bearing on whether an interpretability tool improves feature interpretability. It does not reproduce the Qwen neuron-pole audit.
record.gate_note: The study reports lower average correlation entropy for MedSAE features than raw MedCLIP embeddings, higher density at high interpretation-detection accuracies, and more features above a stated accuracy threshold. These results bear on V4's tool-improvement component. Its composite-image linearity result and SAE sparsity/reconstruction metrics do not directly measure any listed version and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study trains a sparse autoencoder on MedCLIP-ResNet final-layer embeddings. It then compares the SAE's learned dictionary latents with raw embedding dimensions on class-correlation entropy and MedGemma detection accuracy. SAE latents are a trained replacement basis, not the model's own neurons. Comparing them with raw dimensions is the superposition framing the essay disputes, not a better tool for reading neurons. No result measures the share of the model's own neurons with one job, gets better neuron explanations from improved tools or architectures, re-examines canonical neurons, builds neuron circuits, or scores explanations by activation simulation on text. It cites Bills et al. (an original source) only as background for automated naming. The record's link of R1–R3 to V4 rests on treating SAE features as the model's neurons, which V4 does not name.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that MedSAEs extract approximately monosemantic, clinically meaningful features from MedCLIP embeddings, with better correlation and automated-naming interpretability than raw embeddings. They frame this as SAEs disentangling superposition, which they assume, supported only by a linearity sanity check. They note limits: a single MedCLIP-ResNet backbone, sensitivity to which top-activating samples are chosen, need for expert validation, and reliance on the linear representation and superposition hypotheses.
record.recipe_differences: Trains a ReLU SAE on normalized MedCLIP image embeddings and evaluates class-correlation entropy and MedGemma-generated interpretations with image detection, rather than auditing Qwen neuron poles and their job counts.
record.method_sensitivity: Automated naming may be sensitive to the selection of top-activating samples; the authors identify this as a limitation.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE latents trained on MedCLIP-ResNet final-layer embeddings give lower class-correlation entropy (2.25 vs 2.38). They also give more MedGemma-detectable interpretations above 70% accuracy than raw embedding dimensions (21 vs 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In a medical vision-language encoder, SAE dictionary features are more class-selective and more automatically nameable than the raw final-layer embedding dimensions.

fits_no_version.finding: Only 2 of 512 raw MedCLIP embedding dimensions get MedGemma image-detection accuracy above 70%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: With image-based automated naming and detection, very few raw final-layer dimensions of a medical CLIP ResNet receive high-accuracy explanations.

record.problems: Evidence is limited to MedCLIP-ResNet and CheXpert; the authors say automated naming depends on selected top-activating samples and may introduce dataset-specific biases. Human-in-the-loop medical expert validation is still needed. The reported count above 70% concerns the highest-accuracy interpretations, not a stated overall share of all units; detection-accuracy comparisons have no reported uncertainty.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out under the row cap. The composite-image linearity experiment and SAE sparsity/reconstruction measures were not extracted because they do not directly measure a listed claim version.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit or job-count shares.
No language models, no scale or MoE comparison.
No re-examination of InceptionV1 or other canonical polysemantic neurons.
No comparison of architectures or regularization, and no improved tools applied to the model's own neurons; it reports SAE latents only.
No test of explanations fitting activating examples but failing on held-out activations.

record.verdict_notes: I removed the record's V4 'supports' label. SAE latents are a trained replacement basis, so better scores for them do not show that the model's own neurons are interpretable with better tools; if anything the study adopts the superposition view V4 argues against. The record's reader guesses (tests/T2) are overridden. The linearity check (cosine 0.97) and the sparsity/reconstruction metrics bear on no version.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not audit Qwen3-32B neuron poles or report shares with one job, two related jobs, or unknown jobs.
It tests only MedCLIP-ResNet on chest X-rays, not language models, multiple model scales, dense versus MoE models, or trillion-parameter models.
It does not re-examine InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons or test pose, recursive generalization, or superposition as explanations for those examples.

It compares SAE features with raw MedCLIP embeddings, but does not compare architectures, establish why late-layer neurons are messy, or estimate an interpretable-neuron share for InceptionV1-sized vision models.
It does not build attribution graphs or test whether model-native neurons suffice as circuit units.

It evaluates interpretations with an image-detection task, but does not test whether explanations fit their source activating examples while failing to predict neuron activations on held-out examples.

Its MedGemma detection score is not a simulation of neuron activations on new text, and it does not test the claim about the share of neurons receiving good automated explanation scores in that setup.

rows.subject: MedCLIP-ResNet with MedSAE
rows.size_stated: MedCLIP embedding dimension d = 512; SAE expansion rate 16
rows.operation_detail: Compared average entropy of neuron-label correlation distributions for MedSAE neurons and raw MedCLIP embeddings.

conditions.value: MedSAE neurons versus raw MedCLIP embeddings

rows.measure: Average correlation entropy (lower indicates more class-specific neurons)
rows.note: The study reports the comparison as evidence of lower entropy for SAE neurons; it does not report the distribution of individual neuron-pole job counts.
rows.check: The row measures SAE dictionary latents (8192, 30% dead) against raw MedCLIP embedding dimensions. It does not measure how interpretable the model's own neurons become with better tools or architecture, so it does not bear on V4. Also, 2.25 vs 2.38 entropy is a small difference and no uncertainty is reported.

rows.subject: MedCLIP-ResNet with MedSAE
rows.size_stated: MedCLIP embedding dimension d = 512; SAE expansion rate 16
rows.operation_detail: MedGemma detected whether images matched automatically generated feature interpretations.

conditions.value: 30 activating and 30 random non-activating images; sampling with replacement when needed

rows.measure: Number of neuron interpretations with detection accuracy above 70%
rows.note: The paper reports the counts for the highest-accuracy interpretations; it does not state the overall share of all units above the threshold.
rows.check: 21 is a count of distinct interpretations after duplicates were removed, among about 8192 SAE latents. 2 is a count among 512 raw dimensions. The counts are not normalized shares and not neuron-level tool improvements, so the row does not bear on V4. The raw count (2 of 512 above 70%) is a weak-tool reading of the model's own units, but it is image detection by MedGemma, not text simulation (V7).

rows.subject: MedCLIP-ResNet with MedSAE
rows.size_stated: MedCLIP embedding dimension d = 512; SAE expansion rate 16
rows.operation_detail: Compared distributions of MedGemma interpretation-detection accuracy across SAE, raw MedCLIP, and shuffled-pair conditions.

conditions.value: SAE neurons versus raw MedCLIP embeddings and SAE with shuffled neuron-concept pairs

rows.baseline: Raw MedCLIP embeddings and shuffled-pair condition (figure only)
rows.value: Figure only; the text says SAE neurons have noticeably higher density at high detection accuracies than both comparisons
rows.note: The figure provides the distributions; the text describes the qualitative ordering but gives no numeric density values.
rows.check: The row compares density curves of SAE latents, raw dimensions and a shuffled control, read from a figure only. The text says the overall shapes are similar. It measures a replacement basis, not the model's neurons, so it does not bear on V4.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: MedCLIP-ResNet features, comparing MedSAE with raw MedCLIP embeddings on CheXpert
reader_labels.reason: MedSAE features have lower reported correlation entropy, higher density at high detection accuracies, and more interpretations above 70% detection accuracy than raw embeddings (R1–R3). This supports the tool-improvement component, not the version's architecture explanation or its InceptionV1 share estimates.
